ageRules.message: Nigeria's Trade Information Portal lists used motor vehicles above 12 years from manufacture as prohibited, while its vehicle-import guide says less than 15 years. This model year falls outside the stricter prohibition threshold. The official pages conflict; confirm the specific vehicle with Nigeria Customs or a licensed clearing agent before buying.

sourceNotes.name: Nigeria Trade Information Portal - importing motor vehicles
sourceNotes.note: The portal guide says only vehicles less than 15 years from manufacture are permitted. This conflicts with the portal's own prohibited-items list; do not use the guide alone to clear older used vehicles.

sourceNotes.name: Nigeria Trade Information Portal - prohibited items
sourceNotes.note: The official prohibition list says used HS 8703 vehicles above twelve years from manufacture are prohibited. This stricter line is the conservative planning gate pending a Customs clarification of the conflicting guide.

sourceNotes.name: Nigeria Trade Information Portal — observed HS 8703232000 scenario
sourceNotes.note: Synthetic USD 9,000 FOB + 900 freight + 100 insurance: 20% duty, 15% levy, 0.5% ETLS, 7% surcharge on duty,4% FOB FCS,7.5% VAT. Observed VAT excludes the vehicle levy and there is no green-tax line. This reproduces portal arithmetic, not a certification of applicable liability.

sourceNotes.name: Finance Ministry 2026 circular, public USDA attachment
sourceNotes.note: Signed April 1 circular, Annex V (p32):green bands 2% for 2000–3999cc,4% from 4000cc; exclusions include EVs and mass-transit buses. Effective July 1. Annex I (p14) has 20% duty + 20% IAT for listed 8703 codes, conflicting with later notices and portal.

sourceNotes.name: National Assembly Nigeria Tax Act 2025, sections 147 and 149
sourceNotes.note: 7.5% VAT; imported-value base includes import taxes and charges other than VAT. The comparison includes selected charges; declaration-specific exemptions still require confirmation.

sourceNotes.name: Customs Broadcasting Network — June 27 green-tax briefing
sourceNotes.note: Reports vehicle levy 20% to 10% and used-vehicle duties 15% to 5%. Wording does not reconcile with the April schedule or portal; not silently substituted into the dated scenario.

sourceNotes.name: Customs acknowledges 4% FOB suspension, September 16, 2025
sourceNotes.note: Suspension notice conflicts with 4% FCS still displayed by the portal. Custom assumptions allow the applicable FOB charge to be entered without combining CISS and FCS.

disclaimers: Planning scenarios, not an official payable Customs quote. Customs determines classification, valuation, exemptions and the final amount.

The dated portal scenario preserves its observed VAT base and missing green-tax line. The separately labelled statutory-assumption comparison adds the Annex V green band on assumed CIF and includes the vehicle levy in VAT, while retaining the other portal rates; it is not a verified replacement schedule.

For other vehicles choose Custom assumptions and enter the relevant charge rates. Do not add CISS and FCS twice. ECOWAS community-levy exclusions depend on origin and applicable treatment; set 0 only where applicable.

The official trade portal conflicts on used-vehicle age: its prohibition list says above 12 years is prohibited, while its import guide says less than 15 years is permitted. The stricter 12-year line is used as a conservative planning gate; confirm the specific vehicle with Customs or a licensed clearing agent before purchase.

faqs.question: Can I calculate Nigeria if I only know the car price?
faqs.answer: Yes. The calculator treats purchase price as a FOB-style estimate, adds freight and marine insurance, then calculates on CIF. You can switch to FOB or CIF mode when you have cleaner shipping documents.

faqs.question: Why are the two Nigeria scenarios different?
faqs.answer: The November 20 portal observation for HS 8703232000 excludes vehicle levy from its VAT base and shows no green-tax line. The comparison applies the published green band on an assumed CIF base and includes selected import charges in VAT. Official publications conflict on duty, levy and FOB treatment; edit custom assumptions for your declaration instead of treating either total as a Customs bill.

copy.intro: Compare vehicle purchase, shipping and Nigeria import costs using a dated HS-specific portal scenario or your own charge assumptions. Cash cost and Customs valuation are shown separately.
copy.hiddenCosts: Users often miss terminal delivery orders, scanning or examination fees, local registration, demurrage after free days, and FX spread between the quote date and clearing date.
